Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. articles.description: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena.
articles.text: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena. During their visit to the venue, Rovelyn also had a photo with UST’s Koji Buenaflor, who some believe bears a resemblance to the late Rene. “Rene, even if you’re not here, I am still supporting the call for justice for your death. Thank you, UST, for allowing me to have a photo with someone who looks like you. This game’s for you,” Rovelyn said in Filipino in a Facebook post. UST head coach Pido Jarencio, meanwhile, called the moment 'touching' and dedicated the game to Rene. “It was a touching moment earlier. His mother came to us and went to Koji because Koji looks like Rene. She was reminded of Rene, embraced Koji as if he were Rene, and started crying,” Jarencio said. “I simply told her, ‘You are here with us, and we will dedicate all our games to your son, to Rene.’ She was very happy.” “We’re not doing this for show or grandstanding. They came to us and to Koji, and they were reminded of Rene because he looked like their son. So that’s what I could offer them: every game will be dedicated to Rene Baterbonia. That came from our hearts,” he added. How the Rovelyn Baterbonia-Koji Burnaflor interaction unfolded, according to UST head coach Pido Jarencio @gmasportsph pic.twitter.com/Z7oL2z2ctU — JK Carandang (@jk_carandang) September 17, 2026 UST defeated La Salle, 80-75 , to improve to 1-1. Aside from the Baterbonias, the parents of Divine Adili also attended the UAAP game between Ateneo de Manila University and the University of the East on Wednesday. Baterbonia and Adili passed away on June 8 during a team-building incident in Aurora . —JMB GMA News

articles.title: Who was Rene Baterbonia? Rising basketball star who passed in drowning incident
articles.description: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP.
articles.text: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. READ MORE | Ateneo recruit Rene Baterbonia, foreign student athlete Divine Adili die in drowning incident The 6-foot-4 Baterbonia rose to fame in the Palarong Pambansa, where he represented the Davao region with Ateneo de Davao. In the 2025 edition, Baterbonia and fellow rising cager Macky Pelegrino took charge to help the region defeat Western Visayas in the finals and deliver DAVRAA's first-ever Palarong Pambansa basketball title . That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. He was set to suit up for Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP starting in Season 89, where he was expected to work alongside Jared Bahay and Kieffer Alas under head coach Tab Baldwin. —JMB GMA News

articles.description: The Aurora Police Provincial Office said the drowning incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia was “purely accident” based on their initial probe.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Aurora Police Provincial Office said the drowning incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia was “purely accident” based on their initial probe. Acting Aurora Provincial Director Col. Percival Pineda, at a press conference on Tuesday, said that what happened was a “natural accident”. News broke on Monday regarding the deaths of the 6-foot-10 Adili, 21, and the 6-foot-4 Batebonia, 19. “So base po sa ating nakuhang salaysay ng mga kasama niya, ito pong insidente na ito ay talaga pong purely accident. So natural accident po yung pangyayari, hindi po talaga inaasahan, at sa ngayon, wala po tayong nakikitang foul play sa aksidente na ito,” he told reporters. According to the police official, based on their initial findings, the players were having an undisclosed “activity” when the incident happened. “Base po sa salaysay ng ating mga nakausap na kasama nila, meron silang activity kung saan lumalakad yung mga players natin sa dagat, sa may tabing dagat, hanggang hita po yung lalim ng dagat at bigla na lang silang napunta sa malayo na parte,” he said. “Ito po sa parte na nilalakaran nila ay may isang malalim na lugar. At ito nga po, bigla silang tinangay ng current papunta po sa mas malalim na lugar ng dagat.” Pineda, though, bared that the “team activity” has been conducted the past years as well. “Ito po actually ay may mga series na ng ganitong team activity yung grupo na ito. May mga series na po sila, ibig sabihin po hindi lang po ito ngayon lang, may mga nakaraang taon po may mga activities na sila sa nasabing resort din,” he said. “Kaya nga po sa tingin po natin ay alam nila yung sitwasyon sa lugar na yun kaya po ginagawa nila yung usual na activities nila na ito.” Interviews from previous Blue Eagles have gone viral over social media in the past days regarding the Aurora trainings. articles.title: Who was Rene Baterbonia? Rising basketball star who passed in drowning incident
articles.description: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP.
articles.text: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. READ MORE | Ateneo recruit Rene Baterbonia, foreign student athlete Divine Adili die in drowning incident The 6-foot-4 Baterbonia rose to fame in the Palarong Pambansa, where he represented the Davao region with Ateneo de Davao. In the 2025 edition, Baterbonia and fellow rising cager Macky Pelegrino took charge to help the region defeat Western Visayas in the finals and deliver DAVRAA's first-ever Palarong Pambansa basketball title . That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. He was set to suit up for Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP starting in Season 89, where he was expected to work alongside Jared Bahay and Kieffer Alas under head coach Tab Baldwin. —JMB GMA News

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Aurora Police Provincial Office said the drowning incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia was “purely accident” based on their initial probe. Acting Aurora Provincial Director Col. Percival Pineda, at a press conference on Tuesday, said that what happened was a “natural accident”. News broke on Monday regarding the deaths of the 6-foot-10 Adili, 21, and the 6-foot-4 Batebonia, 19. “So base po sa ating nakuhang salaysay ng mga kasama niya, ito pong insidente na ito ay talaga pong purely accident. So natural accident po yung pangyayari, hindi po talaga inaasahan, at sa ngayon, wala po tayong nakikitang foul play sa aksidente na ito,” he told reporters. According to the police official, based on their initial findings, the players were having an undisclosed “activity” when the incident happened. “Base po sa salaysay ng ating mga nakausap na kasama nila, meron silang activity kung saan lumalakad yung mga players natin sa dagat, sa may tabing dagat, hanggang hita po yung lalim ng dagat at bigla na lang silang napunta sa malayo na parte,” he said. “Ito po sa parte na nilalakaran nila ay may isang malalim na lugar. articles.description: Rene Baterbonia was laid to rest Thursday with his name now immortalized in Talacogon, Agusan del Sur and across the country.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Rene Baterbonia was laid to rest Thursday with his name now immortalized in Talacogon, Agusan del Sur and across the country. Thousands of people lined up during the funeral around the town on the way to newly established Barangay Labnig Memorial Cemetery, where families, friends and relatives bid goodbye to the Tacalogon’s son. text.preview: Sebastian Duterte personally covered the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia from Manila to Agusan del Sur. At least 13 Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte covered all the expenses in transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) Blue Eagles cager Rene “Bobet” Baterbonia to his hometown in Agusan del Sur. These are false. The earliest copy of the post from an FB user, with a graphic containing a side-by-side photo of Baterbonia and Duterte, was published on June 20. He said: “We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Sebastian ‘Baste’ Duterte for extending assistance from Manila to Davao and all the way to Talacogon. Your support helped ease the burden on Rene’s family and ensured that he was brought home with dignity and honor. – Coach Jess” While the local government of Davao City helped with the accommodation, food, and transportation of Baterbonia’s family from Davao City to Agusan del Sur, it was Ateneo that provided the plane to transport the remains of the student-athlete. article.text: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. articles.text: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena. During their visit to the venue, Rovelyn also had a photo with UST’s Koji Buenaflor, who some believe bears a resemblance to the late Rene. “Rene, even if you’re not here, I am still supporting the call for justice for your death. Thank you, UST, for allowing me to have a photo with someone who looks like you. This game’s for you,” Rovelyn said in Filipino in a Facebook post. UST head coach Pido Jarencio, meanwhile, called the moment 'touching' and dedicated the game to Rene. “It was a touching moment earlier. His mother came to us and went to Koji because Koji looks like Rene. She was reminded of Rene, embraced Koji as if he were Rene, and started crying,” Jarencio said. “I simply told her, ‘You are here with us, and we will dedicate all our games to your son, to Rene.’ She was very happy.” “We’re not doing this for show or grandstanding. They came to us and to Koji, and they were reminded of Rene because he looked like their son. So that’s what I could offer them: every game will be dedicated to Rene Baterbonia. That came from our hearts,” he added. How the Rovelyn Baterbonia-Koji Burnaflor interaction unfolded, according to UST head coach Pido Jarencio @gmasportsph pic.twitter.com/Z7oL2z2ctU — JK Carandang (@jk_carandang) September 17, 2026 UST defeated La Salle, 80-75 , to improve to 1-1. Aside from the Baterbonias, the parents of Divine Adili also attended the UAAP game between Ateneo de Manila University and the University of the East on Wednesday. Baterbonia and Adili passed away on June 8 during a team-building incident in Aurora . —JMB GMA News

articles.title: Who was Rene Baterbonia? Rising basketball star who passed in drowning incident
articles.description: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP.
articles.text: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. READ MORE | Ateneo recruit Rene Baterbonia, foreign student athlete Divine Adili die in drowning incident The 6-foot-4 Baterbonia rose to fame in the Palarong Pambansa, where he represented the Davao region with Ateneo de Davao. In the 2025 edition, Baterbonia and fellow rising cager Macky Pelegrino took charge to help the region defeat Western Visayas in the finals and deliver DAVRAA's first-ever Palarong Pambansa basketball title . That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. He was set to suit up for Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP starting in Season 89, where he was expected to work alongside Jared Bahay and Kieffer Alas under head coach Tab Baldwin. —JMB GMA News

At least 13 Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte covered all the expenses in transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) Blue Eagles cager Rene “Bobet” Baterbonia to his hometown in Agusan del Sur.
These are false.
The earliest copy of the post from an FB user, with a graphic containing a side-by-side photo of Baterbonia and Duterte, was published on June 20.

😭😭) The claim was further bolstered with the inclusion of a portion of Ateneo de Davao’s basketball coach Jess Evangelio’s statement expressing his gratitude to Duterte and the local government of Davao City.

He said: “We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Sebastian ‘Baste’ Duterte for extending assistance from Manila to Davao and all the way to Talacogon. ADMU also shouldered all of the wake and funeral expenses for the late student.

Evangelio was thanking the local officials of Davao for providing food, transportation, accommodation, and security assistance to the bereaved family and supporters.
The basketball coach is a Davao City native and is known for mentoring award-winning basketball players.

The misleading posts surfaced after the Baterbonia family’s press conference on June 10.
His mother initially sought help from government officials to fly the remains, before ADMU arranged for a private plane.

MANILA — Rene Baterbonia was not, in any way, connected to University of Santo Tomas before his passing, but it was with the España-based team that his bereaved family found solace as they continue to cope with their loss.
Rene’s parents, Rovelyn Baterbonia and Rene Baterbonia Sr., were present at the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball matches on Wednesday and visited UST ahead of its game against De La Salle University.

Growling Tigers head coach Pido Jarencio revealed that the Baterbonias decided to visit the team after Rovelyn found comfort in seeing UST forward Koji Buenaflor, whom the family felt bore similarities to Rene.
“Yung mother, pumunta sa amin,” said Jarencio after their 80-75 win over La Salle.
“Pumunta kay Koji kasi parang lookalike ni Rene. Niyakap, umiiyak yung nanay.”

The Baterbonias were already in attendance at the Mall of Asia Arena earlier in the day as Ateneo de Manila University — the school that had committed to Rene well before the June 8 tragedy in Dipaculao, Aurora — dominated University of the East, 101-74.

It was also around that time that they visited UST’s dugout.
“Hindi kami pumapapel, or nag ga-grandstanding, basta pinuntahan kami,” shared Jarencio.
“Si Koji, naaalala nila na parang anak nila, kaya kami naman, yun lang ang nao-offer namin sa kanila.”
After the Baterbonias shared moments with the Growling Tigers, Jarencio said UST would dedicate its UAAP Season 89 campaign to the family.
“Sinabi ko lang naman sa kanya, nandito kayo, ide-dedicate namin lahat ng games namin para sa anak niyo, kay Rene, so tuwang-tuwa yung nanay,” shared Jarencio.

The parents of Divine Adili, Elias and Ifeoma, were also in attendance during the Ateneo-UE match.

passages.text: University of Santo Tomas head coach Pido Jarencio (left) and the Baterbonia family in UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball.
UAAP Media.

MANILA — Rene Baterbonia was not, in any way, connected to University of Santo Tomas before his passing, but it was with the España-based team that his bereaved family found solace as they continue to cope with their loss.
Rene’s parents, Rovelyn Baterbonia and Rene Baterbonia Sr., were present at the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball matches on Wednesday and visited UST ahead of its game against De La Salle University.

Growling Tigers head coach Pido Jarencio revealed that the Baterbonias decided to visit the team after Rovelyn found comfort in seeing UST forward Koji Buenaflor, whom the family felt bore similarities to Rene.
“Yung mother, pumunta sa amin,” said Jarencio after their 80-75 win over La Salle.
“Pumunta kay Koji kasi parang lookalike ni Rene. Niyakap, umiiyak yung nanay.”

The Baterbonias were already in attendance at the Mall of Asia Arena earlier in the day as Ateneo de Manila University — the school that had committed to Rene well before the June 8 tragedy in Dipaculao, Aurora — dominated University of the East, 101-74.
However, before the UST-La Salle match, the Baterbonias moved from the lower box section to the seats behind the Tigers’ bench.
It was also around that time that they visited UST’s dugout.
“Hindi kami pumapapel, or nag ga-grandstanding, basta pinuntahan kami,” shared Jarencio.
“Si Koji, naaalala nila na parang anak nila, kaya kami naman, yun lang ang nao-offer namin sa kanila.”
After the Baterbonias shared moments with the Growling Tigers, Jarencio said UST would dedicate its UAAP Season 89 campaign to the family.
“Sinabi ko lang naman sa kanya, nandito kayo, ide-dedicate namin lahat ng games namin para sa anak niyo, kay Rene, so tuwang-tuwa yung nanay,” shared Jarencio.
“Every game is dedicated kay Rene Baterbonia. We’re not from Ateneo, basta kami, sarili namin, sa puso namin nanggaling yun,” he added.
The Ateneo Blue Eagles have also dedicated their campaign to the Baterbonia and Adili families, with the players donning jerseys bearing patches of their initials, “DA | RB.”
The parents of Divine Adili, Elias and Ifeoma, were also in attendance during the Ateneo-UE match.

articles.text: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena. During their visit to the venue, Rovelyn also had a photo with UST’s Koji Buenaflor, who some believe bears a resemblance to the late Rene. “Rene, even if you’re not here, I am still supporting the call for justice for your death. Thank you, UST, for allowing me to have a photo with someone who looks like you. This game’s for you,” Rovelyn said in Filipino in a Facebook post. UST head coach Pido Jarencio, meanwhile, called the moment 'touching' and dedicated the game to Rene. “It was a touching moment earlier. His mother came to us and went to Koji because Koji looks like Rene. She was reminded of Rene, embraced Koji as if he were Rene, and started crying,” Jarencio said. “I simply told her, ‘You are here with us, and we will dedicate all our games to your son, to Rene.’ She was very happy.” “We’re not doing this for show or grandstanding. They came to us and to Koji, and they were reminded of Rene because he looked like their son. So that’s what I could offer them: every game will be dedicated to Rene Baterbonia. That came from our hearts,” he added. How the Rovelyn Baterbonia-Koji Burnaflor interaction unfolded, according to UST head coach Pido Jarencio @gmasportsph pic.twitter.com/Z7oL2z2ctU — JK Carandang (@jk_carandang) September 17, 2026 UST defeated La Salle, 80-75 , to improve to 1-1. Aside from the Baterbonias, the parents of Divine Adili also attended the UAAP game between Ateneo de Manila University and the University of the East on Wednesday. Baterbonia and Adili passed away on June 8 during a team-building incident in Aurora . —JMB GMA News

Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. READ MORE | Ateneo recruit Rene Baterbonia, foreign student athlete Divine Adili die in drowning incident The 6-foot-4 Baterbonia rose to fame in the Palarong Pambansa, where he represented the Davao region with Ateneo de Davao. In the 2025 edition, Baterbonia and fellow rising cager Macky Pelegrino took charge to help the region defeat Western Visayas in the finals and deliver DAVRAA's first-ever Palarong Pambansa basketball title . That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. He was set to suit up for Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP starting in Season 89, where he was expected to work alongside Jared Bahay and Kieffer Alas under head coach Tab Baldwin. —JMB GMA News

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Aurora Police Provincial Office said the drowning incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia was “purely accident” based on their initial probe. Acting Aurora Provincial Director Col. Percival Pineda, at a press conference on Tuesday, said that what happened was a “natural accident”. News broke on Monday regarding the deaths of the 6-foot-10 Adili, 21, and the 6-foot-4 Batebonia, 19. “So base po sa ating nakuhang salaysay ng mga kasama niya, ito pong insidente na ito ay talaga pong purely accident. So natural accident po yung pangyayari, hindi po talaga inaasahan, at sa ngayon, wala po tayong nakikitang foul play sa aksidente na ito,” he told reporters. According to the police official, based on their initial findings, the players were having an undisclosed “activity” when the incident happened. “Base po sa salaysay ng ating mga nakausap na kasama nila, meron silang activity kung saan lumalakad yung mga players natin sa dagat, sa may tabing dagat, hanggang hita po yung lalim ng dagat at bigla na lang silang napunta sa malayo na parte,” he said. “Ito po sa parte na nilalakaran nila ay may isang malalim na lugar. At ito nga po, bigla silang tinangay ng current papunta po sa mas malalim na lugar ng dagat.” Pineda, though, bared that the “team activity” has been conducted the past years as well. “Ito po actually ay may mga series na ng ganitong team activity yung grupo na ito. May mga series na po sila, ibig sabihin po hindi lang po ito ngayon lang, may mga nakaraang taon po may mga activities na sila sa nasabing resort din,” he said. “Kaya nga po sa tingin po natin ay alam nila yung sitwasyon sa lugar na yun kaya po ginagawa nila yung usual na activities nila na ito.” Interviews from previous Blue Eagles have gone viral over social media in the past days regarding the Aurora trainings. MANILA, Philippines — Rene Baterbonia was laid to rest Thursday with his name now immortalized in Talacogon, Agusan del Sur and across the country. Thousands of people lined up during the funeral around the town on the way to newly established Barangay Labnig Memorial Cemetery, where families, friends and relatives bid goodbye to the Tacalogon’s son. At the center of it all was his parents wearing his Davao Region Athletic Association (DAVRAA) jersey No. 2, which was retired by his alma mater Ateneo de Davao University. Baterbonia, 18, passed away on June 8 with Ateneo de Manila University teammate Divine Adili from Nigeria in a tragic drowning incident during the Blue Eagles’ team-building activity in Dipaculao, Aurora. He just arrived in Manila that week after his senior high school graduation from the Ateneo de Davao, which he led to multiple regional titles including the Davao Region’s first-ever Palarong Pambansa title in 2025 in Laoag where he was named as the MVP. This year, Baterbonia had a homecoming in Agusan del Sur that served as first-time Palaro host albeit Davao Region yielded the throne to CALABARZON. Hopes were high for Baterbonia as one of the country’s rising stars, especially with the glorious Ateneo program in the UAAP, before his unfortunate demise that led to a national outcry and a massive government probe. Talacogon on the same day adopted an ordinance declaring June 8 as “Rene Clert ‘Bobet’ N. Baterbonia Day” in honor of his legacy and contributions to the local government unit through sports. Aside from the ordinance, Ateneo de Davao has also renamed its Senior High School courts as the “Rene Bobet Baterbonia Covered Courts”. Calls for the Department of Education (DepEd) to name the Palarong Pambansa MVP to a former awardee himself have also gained traction. articles.text: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena. During their visit to the venue, Rovelyn also had a photo with UST’s Koji Buenaflor, who some believe bears a resemblance to the late Rene. “Rene, even if you’re not here, I am still supporting the call for justice for your death. Thank you, UST, for allowing me to have a photo with someone who looks like you. This game’s for you,” Rovelyn said in Filipino in a Facebook post. UST head coach Pido Jarencio, meanwhile, called the moment 'touching' and dedicated the game to Rene. “It was a touching moment earlier. His mother came to us and went to Koji because Koji looks like Rene. She was reminded of Rene, embraced Koji as if he were Rene, and started crying,” Jarencio said. “I simply told her, ‘You are here with us, and we will dedicate all our games to your son, to Rene.’ She was very happy.” “We’re not doing this for show or grandstanding. They came to us and to Koji, and they were reminded of Rene because he looked like their son. So that’s what I could offer them: every game will be dedicated to Rene Baterbonia. That came from our hearts,” he added. How the Rovelyn Baterbonia-Koji Burnaflor interaction unfolded, according to UST head coach Pido Jarencio @gmasportsph pic.twitter.com/Z7oL2z2ctU — JK Carandang (@jk_carandang) September 17, 2026 UST defeated La Salle, 80-75 , to improve to 1-1. Aside from the Baterbonias, the parents of Divine Adili also attended the UAAP game between Ateneo de Manila University and the University of the East on Wednesday. Baterbonia and Adili passed away on June 8 during a team-building incident in Aurora . —JMB GMA News

Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. READ MORE | Ateneo recruit Rene Baterbonia, foreign student athlete Divine Adili die in drowning incident The 6-foot-4 Baterbonia rose to fame in the Palarong Pambansa, where he represented the Davao region with Ateneo de Davao. In the 2025 edition, Baterbonia and fellow rising cager Macky Pelegrino took charge to help the region defeat Western Visayas in the finals and deliver DAVRAA's first-ever Palarong Pambansa basketball title . That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. He was set to suit up for Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP starting in Season 89, where he was expected to work alongside Jared Bahay and Kieffer Alas under head coach Tab Baldwin. —JMB GMA News

Acting Aurora Provincial Director Col. Percival Pineda, at a press conference on Tuesday, said that what happened was a “natural accident”. News broke on Monday regarding the deaths of the 6-foot-10 Adili, 21, and the 6-foot-4 Batebonia, 19. “So base po sa ating nakuhang salaysay ng mga kasama niya, ito pong insidente na ito ay talaga pong purely accident. So natural accident po yung pangyayari, hindi po talaga inaasahan, at sa ngayon, wala po tayong nakikitang foul play sa aksidente na ito,” he told reporters. article.description: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena.
article.text: Rene Baterbonia’s mom, Rovelyn, was on the sidelines of the UAAP Season 89 game between the University of Santo Tomas and De La Salle University on Wednesday at the Mall of Asia Arena. During their visit to the venue, Rovelyn also had a photo with UST’s Koji Buenaflor, who some believe bears a resemblance to the late Rene. “Rene, even if you’re not here, I am still supporting the call for justice for your death. Thank you, UST, for allowing me to have a photo with someone who looks like you. This game’s for you,” Rovelyn said in Filipino in a Facebook post. UST head coach Pido Jarencio, meanwhile, called the moment 'touching' and dedicated the game to Rene. “It was a touching moment earlier. His mother came to us and went to Koji because Koji looks like Rene. She was reminded of Rene, embraced Koji as if he were Rene, and started crying,” Jarencio said. “I simply told her, ‘You are here with us, and we will dedicate all our games to your son, to Rene.’ She was very happy.” “We’re not doing this for show or grandstanding. They came to us and to Koji, and they were reminded of Rene because he looked like their son. So that’s what I could offer them: every game will be dedicated to Rene Baterbonia. That came from our hearts,” he added. article.title: Who was Rene Baterbonia? Rising basketball star who passed in drowning incident
article.description: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP.
article.text: Rene Baterbonia was poised to begin the next chapter of his promising basketball career with Ateneo de Manila University in the UAAP. But before Baterbonia could don the Blue Eagles jersey, his journey was tragically cut short following a drowning incident that also claimed the life of fellow student-athlete Divine Adili. According to Ateneo, Baterbonia and Adili passed away during a team building on Monday in Dipaculao, Aurora. Baterbonia was 18 while Adili was 21. READ MORE | Ateneo recruit Rene Baterbonia, foreign student athlete Divine Adili die in drowning incident The 6-foot-4 Baterbonia rose to fame in the Palarong Pambansa, where he represented the Davao region with Ateneo de Davao. In the 2025 edition, Baterbonia and fellow rising cager Macky Pelegrino took charge to help the region defeat Western Visayas in the finals and deliver DAVRAA's first-ever Palarong Pambansa basketball title . That same edition included an MVP award and a Mythical Five selection for him. He was also part of the team that clinched a gold medal in the 14th ASEAN School Games in Brunei in November 2025. Ateneo de Davao returned with the same grit in 2026 Palarong Pambansa in Baterbonia's hometown, Agusan del Sur. The defending champions once again reached the finals but eventually lost to Region IV-A to miss out on the back-to-back titles. Still, Baterbonia left the Palarong Pambansa with a lasting legacy. He was set to suit up for Ateneo Blue Eagles in the UAAP starting in Season 89, where he was expected to work alongside Jared Bahay and Kieffer Alas under head coach Tab Baldwin. —JMB GMA News

article.description: The Aurora Police Provincial Office said the drowning incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia was “purely accident” based on their initial probe.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Aurora Police Provincial Office said the drowning incident involving Ateneo Blue Eagles Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia was “purely accident” based on their initial probe. Acting Aurora Provincial Director Col. Percival Pineda, at a press conference on Tuesday, said that what happened was a “natural accident”. News broke on Monday regarding the deaths of the 6-foot-10 Adili, 21, and the 6-foot-4 Batebonia, 19. “So base po sa ating nakuhang salaysay ng mga kasama niya, ito pong insidente na ito ay talaga pong purely accident. So natural accident po yung pangyayari, hindi po talaga inaasahan, at sa ngayon, wala po tayong nakikitang foul play sa aksidente na ito,” he told reporters. According to the police official, based on their initial findings, the players were having an undisclosed “activity” when the incident happened. “Base po sa salaysay ng ating mga nakausap na kasama nila, meron silang activity kung saan lumalakad yung mga players natin sa dagat, sa may tabing dagat, hanggang hita po yung lalim ng dagat at bigla na lang silang napunta sa malayo na parte,” he said. “Ito po sa parte na nilalakaran nila ay may isang malalim na lugar. At ito nga po, bigla silang tinangay ng current papunta po sa mas malalim na lugar ng dagat.” Pineda, though, bared that the “team activity” has been conducted the past years as well. “Ito po actually ay may mga series na ng ganitong team activity yung grupo na ito. article.title: Baterbonia laid to rest
article.description: Rene Baterbonia was laid to rest Thursday with his name now immortalized in Talacogon, Agusan del Sur and across the country.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Rene Baterbonia was laid to rest Thursday with his name now immortalized in Talacogon, Agusan del Sur and across the country. Thousands of people lined up during the funeral around the town on the way to newly established Barangay Labnig Memorial Cemetery, where families, friends and relatives bid goodbye to the Tacalogon’s son. At the center of it all was his parents wearing his Davao Region Athletic Association (DAVRAA) jersey No. 2, which was retired by his alma mater Ateneo de Davao University. Baterbonia, 18, passed away on June 8 with Ateneo de Manila University teammate Divine Adili from Nigeria in a tragic drowning incident during the Blue Eagles’ team-building activity in Dipaculao, Aurora. He just arrived in Manila that week after his senior high school graduation from the Ateneo de Davao, which he led to multiple regional titles including the Davao Region’s first-ever Palarong Pambansa title in 2025 in Laoag where he was named as the MVP. This year, Baterbonia had a homecoming in Agusan del Sur that served as first-time Palaro host albeit Davao Region yielded the throne to CALABARZON. Hopes were high for Baterbonia as one of the country’s rising stars, especially with the glorious Ateneo program in the UAAP, before his unfortunate demise that led to a national outcry and a massive government probe. Talacogon on the same day adopted an ordinance declaring June 8 as “Rene Clert ‘Bobet’ N. Baterbonia Day” in honor of his legacy and contributions to the local government unit through sports. Aside from the ordinance, Ateneo de Davao has also renamed its Senior High School courts as the “Rene Bobet Baterbonia Covered Courts”. Calls for the Department of Education (DepEd) to name the Palarong Pambansa MVP to a former awardee himself have also gained traction. MANILA — Rene Baterbonia was not, in any way, connected to University of Santo Tomas before his passing, but it was with the España-based team that his bereaved family found solace as they continue to cope with their loss. Growling Tigers head coach Pido Jarencio revealed that the Baterbonias decided to visit the team after Rovelyn found comfort in seeing UST forward Koji Buenaflor, whom the family felt bore similarities to Rene. “Yung mother, pumunta sa amin,” said Jarencio after their 80-75 win over La Salle. “Pumunta kay Koji kasi parang lookalike ni Rene. Niyakap, umiiyak yung nanay.” The Baterbonias were already in attendance at the Mall of Asia Arena earlier in the day as Ateneo de Manila University — the school that had committed to Rene well before the June 8 tragedy in Dipaculao, Aurora — dominated University of the East, 101-74. However, before the UST-La Salle match, the Baterbonias moved from the lower box section to the seats behind the Tigers’ bench. It was also around that time that they visited UST’s dugout. “Hindi kami pumapapel, or nag ga-grandstanding, basta pinuntahan kami,” shared Jarencio. “Si Koji, naaalala nila na parang anak nila, kaya kami naman, yun lang ang nao-offer namin sa kanila.” After the Baterbonias shared moments with the Growling Tigers, Jarencio said UST would dedicate its UAAP Season 89 campaign to the family. “Sinabi ko lang naman sa kanya, nandito kayo, ide-dedicate namin lahat ng games namin para sa anak niyo, kay Rene, so tuwang-tuwa yung nanay,” shared Jarencio. “Every game is dedicated kay Rene Baterbonia. text.preview: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passed a resolution on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, conferring the Datu Lipus Makapandong Award upon Baterbonia in recognition posthumously of his outstanding achievements, exemplary contributions to basketball, and for bringing honor, prestige, and pride to the province. In the resolution, the provincial government also announced the official retirement of Jersey Number 2 in honor of Baterbonia. The resolution said that the jersey number shall no longer be assigned, worn, or issued to any player participating in Governor’s Cup games and other provincial government-sponsored or sanctioned basketball competitions in Agusan del Sur. The legislative measure added that Baterbonia’s life, achievements, and enduring legacy be permanently recorded in the annals of the province as an example of excellence, discipline, perseverance, humility, leadership, and dedication to sports, serving as an inspiration to present and future generations of Agusanon athletes. Officials ordered furnishing and presentation of a copy of the resolution and a plaque of recognition to Baterbonia’s bereaved family as an expression of the provincial government’s gratitude, admiration, respect, and condolences. The resolution highlighted Baterbonia’s basketball career, including his Most Valuable Player (MVP) award at the Palarong Pambansa 2025 and his role in securing a gold medal for the Philippine team at the ASEAN School Games 2025 in Brunei Darussalam. output.title: FACT CHECK: Baste Duterte did NOT cover transport costs of Baterbonia’s remains
output.description: Multiple Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte covered all the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia to Agusan del Sur. These posts are false.

text.preview: Sebastian Duterte personally covered the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia from Manila to Agusan del Sur. Ateneo de Manila University provided the private plane to transport the remains of Baterbonia and shouldered funeral and wake expenses. The local government of Davao City, not Duterte, extended assistance for his family’s other needs. articles.description: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage.

text.preview: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passed a resolution on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, conferring the Datu Lipus Makapandong Award upon Baterbonia in recognition posthumously of his outstanding achievements, exemplary contributions to basketball, and for bringing honor, prestige, and pride to the province. In the resolution, the provincial government also announced the official retirement of Jersey Number 2 in honor of Baterbonia. The resolution said that the jersey number shall no longer be assigned, worn, or issued to any player participating in Governor’s Cup games and other provincial government-sponsored or sanctioned basketball competitions in Agusan del Sur. The legislative measure added that Baterbonia’s life, achievements, and enduring legacy be permanently recorded in the annals of the province as an example of excellence, discipline, perseverance, humility, leadership, and dedication to sports, serving as an inspiration to present and future generations of Agusanon athletes. Officials ordered furnishing and presentation of a copy of the resolution and a plaque of recognition to Baterbonia’s bereaved family as an expression of the provincial government’s gratitude, admiration, respect, and condolences. The resolution highlighted Baterbonia’s basketball career, including his Most Valuable Player (MVP) award at the Palarong Pambansa 2025 and his role in securing a gold medal for the Philippine team at the ASEAN School Games 2025 in Brunei Darussalam. articles.description: Viral posts linking student-athlete Rene Baterbonia's death to a forensic report claims blunt-force traumatic injuries were the cause of death. This is not true.

text.preview: Forensic findings of Rene Baterbonia showing paddle marks, a swollen scrotum, self-defense injuries, and blunt-force traumatic injuries from hazing as cause of death. articles.title: FACT CHECK: Baste Duterte did NOT cover transport costs of Baterbonia’s remains
articles.description: Multiple Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte covered all the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia to Agusan del Sur. These posts are false.

text.preview: Sebastian Duterte personally covered the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia from Manila to Agusan del Sur. Ateneo de Manila University provided the private plane to transport the remains of Baterbonia and shouldered funeral and wake expenses. The local government of Davao City, not Duterte, extended assistance for his family’s other needs. At least 13 Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte covered all the expenses in transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) Blue Eagles cager Rene “Bobet” Baterbonia to his hometown in Agusan del Sur. These are false. The earliest copy of the post from an FB user, with a graphic containing a side-by-side photo of Baterbonia and Duterte, was published on June 20. The caption reads: “ HINDI PALA DAW ATENEO ANG SUMAGOT PARA MAIUWI ANG MGA LABI NI RENE BATERBONIA SA TALACOGON 😭” (So it turns out that Ateneo wasn’t the one who covered the expenses to bring Rene Baterbonia’s remains home to Talacogon. 😭😭) The claim was further bolstered with the inclusion of a portion of Ateneo de Davao’s basketball coach Jess Evangelio’s statement expressing his gratitude to Duterte and the local government of Davao City. He said: “We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Sebastian ‘Baste’ Duterte for extending assistance from Manila to Davao and all the way to Talacogon. Your support helped ease the burden on Rene’s family and ensured that he was brought home with dignity and honor. – Coach Jess” While the local government of Davao City helped with the accommodation, food, and transportation of Baterbonia’s family from Davao City to Agusan del Sur, it was Ateneo that provided the plane to transport the remains of the student-athlete. According to Baterbonia’s lawyer, Israelito Torreo, the private aircraft was provided by Ateneo and the family thanked the school for it. ADMU also shouldered all of the wake and funeral

text.preview: University of Santo Tomas head coach Pido Jarencio (left) and the Baterbonia family in UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball. UAAP Media. MANILA — Rene Baterbonia was not, in any way, connected to University of Santo Tomas before his passing, but it was with the España-based team that his bereaved family found solace as they continue to cope with their loss. Rene’s parents, Rovelyn Baterbonia and Rene Baterbonia Sr., were present at the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball matches on Wednesday and visited UST ahead of its game against De La Salle University. Growling Tigers head coach Pido Jarencio revealed that the Baterbonias decided to visit the team after Rovelyn found comfort in seeing UST forward Koji Buenaflor, whom the family felt bore similarities to Rene. “Yung mother, pumunta sa amin,” said Jarencio after their 80-75 win over La Salle. “Pumunta kay Koji kasi parang lookalike ni Rene. Niyakap, umiiyak yung nanay.” The Baterbonias were already in attendance at the Mall of Asia Arena earlier in the day as Ateneo de Manila University — the school that had committed to Rene well before the June 8 tragedy in Dipaculao, Aurora — dominated University of the East, 101-74. However, before the UST-La Salle match, the Baterbonias moved from the lower box section to the seats behind the Tigers’ bench. It was also around that time that they visited UST’s dugout. “Hindi kami pumapapel, or nag ga-grandstanding, basta pinuntahan kami,” shared Jarencio. “Si Koji, naaalala nila na parang anak nila, kaya kami naman, yun lang ang nao-offer namin sa kanila.” After the Baterbonias shared moments with the Growling Tigers, Jarencio said UST would dedicate its UAAP Season 89 campaign to the family. “Sinabi ko lang naman sa kanya, nandito kayo, ide-dedicate namin lahat ng games namin para sa anak niyo, kay Rene, so tuwang-tuwa yung nanay,” shared Jarencio. “Every game is dedicated kay Rene Baterbonia. text.preview: Ateneo de Davao University basketball coach Jess Evangelio wrote on his Facebook page that four of Rene Baterbonia's former teammates, Macky Pellegrino, Matt Cayetano, Rhysus Bajenting, and JM Sanoria, originally set to transfer to Ateneo De Manila University, have decided to take their talents to De La Salle Zobel. "It is with great pride and gratitude that I finally confirm that our boys will be joining La Salle Zobel as they begin an exciting new chapter in their basketball and academic journey. "We are truly thankful to La Salle Zobel for opening its doors and providing them with the opportunity to grow not only as athletes, but also as students and young men of character. Your trust and belief in their potential mean so much to all of us. "We do not take this opportunity lightly. Our boys are committed to working hard, staying humble, and representing the Lasallian community with pride, discipline, and integrity both on and off the court. "A special thank you to Coach Gian Nazario for believing in them and for playing a significant role in helping shape their future. We are honored to entrust our boys to your program. The journey continues. Animo! "Thank you also Phenom Management Head Coach Brody for always being there for us." RELATED CONTENT: In Memoriam: Divine Adili and Rene Baterbonia's basketball journeys The announcement comes weeks after Coach Jess mourned the passing of Rene Baterbonia , a former Ateneo de Davao standout who was set to join the Ateneo Blue Eagles in the University Athletic Association of the Philippines (UAAP) season this year. Rene Baterbonia and fellow incoming Ateneo Blue Eagles player Divine Adili passed away during a team activity in Dipaculao, Aurora, a tragedy that deeply affected the Philippine basketball community. Despite the loss, Rene's former teammates are moving forward with their basketball aspirations as they prepare to represent De La Salle Zobel in the coming basketball season. articles.title: AgSur names Baterbonia ‘Sports Icon,’ retires No. 2 jersey
articles.description: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage.

text.preview: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passed a resolution on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, conferring the Datu Lipus Makapandong Award upon Baterbonia in recognition posthumously of his outstanding achievements, exemplary contributions to basketball, and for bringing honor, prestige, and pride to the province. In the resolution, the provincial government also announced the official retirement of Jersey Number 2 in honor of Baterbonia. The resolution said that the jersey number shall no longer be assigned, worn, or issued to any player participating in Governor’s Cup games and other provincial government-sponsored or sanctioned basketball competitions in Agusan del Sur. The legislative measure added that Baterbonia’s life, achievements, and enduring legacy be permanently recorded in the annals of the province as an example of excellence, discipline, perseverance, humility, leadership, and dedication to sports, serving as an inspiration to present and future generations of Agusanon athletes. Officials ordered furnishing and presentation of a copy of the resolution and a plaque of recognition to Baterbonia’s bereaved family as an expression of the provincial government’s gratitude, admiration, respect, and condolences. The resolution highlighted Baterbonia’s basketball career, including his Most Valuable Player (MVP) award at the Palarong Pambansa 2025 and his role in securing a gold medal for the Philippine team at the ASEAN School Games 2025 in Brunei Darussalam. articles.title: Ateneo urged to support late cager Rene Baterbonia's siblings
articles.description: The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Cebu has urged Ateneo de Manila University to help secure the education of the surviving siblings of late student-athlete Rene Baterbonia following the accident that resulted in his death.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Cebu has urged Ateneo de Manila University to help secure the education of the surviving siblings of late student-athlete Rene Baterbonia following the accident that resulted in his death. In a statement issued on June 10, Cebu Archbishop Alberto Uy said that helping ensure the continuation of the siblings' education would be a "fitting tribute" to the dreams of the young man who died during a recent team-building tragedy. "I am confident that the leadership of Ateneo de Manila University also grieves over this heartbreaking loss and shares the desire to seek the truth and accompany the family during this painful journey. Beyond words, concrete acts of solidarity can help ease the burden of those left behind," Uy said. "One meaningful way of honoring Rene's memory would be for Ateneo to help ensure that his siblings are able to complete their education. Those who knew Rene describe him as a young man who dreamed not only for himself but also for the well-being and future of his loved ones. To help fulfill that dream would be a fitting tribute to his life, generosity, and sacrifice," he added. The prelate stressed the need to provide the bereaved family with clear and accurate answers regarding the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. "While no explanation can ever bring Rene back, honesty and transparency can help provide a measure of peace and closure to those who mourn him. If lapses or mistakes were committed, a sincere acknowledgment and apology would be an important step toward healing and rebuilding trust," Uy said. "As we seek truth, accountability, and healing, let us also not forget the power of prayer. Let us pray for the eternal repose of Rene's soul, for healing and strength within the Ateneo community, and for comfort, consolation, and hope for the bereaved Baterbonia family during this time of profound grief," he added. text.preview: A seller of Japanese goods is donating part of its profits to the family of the late Atenean recruit Rene Clert “Bobet” Baterbonia . Tokyo Treasures , which claims to sell authentic, high-quality goods sourced from Japan, announced it is giving P500 for every watch sold in June to the Baterbonia family as they cope with the aftermath of their son’s death. The business said it is their “small gesture of support for his family,” lamenting Baterbonia’s death, whom they said was a “young athlete with a bright future.” “Whether it’s a Seiko, Grand Seiko, G-Shock, Citizen, or any watch from our collection, a portion of every successful sale will go directly to Rene’s family,” the shop said in an announcement on Thursday, June 11. “This is not a marketing campaign. This is simply our way of giving back and extending help during a difficult time,” the business added. The business also defended its initiative in the comments section, saying it was not “milking” Baterbonia’s death for profit. “Hindi namin ‘pinagkakakitaan’ ‘yung pagkamatay ng bata. We were already selling watches before this happened, and we will continue selling watches after. The difference now is that part of our earnings will go directly to Rene’s family to help during a difficult time,” it said. “Fundraising through businesses has existed for YEARS. Restaurants, brands, sports teams, and even international companies do donation drives tied to sales because it helps raise bigger amounts using their platform and audience. Hindi porket business ‘yung tumutulong, ‘marketing strategy’ agad,” it added. “If helping while using our reach means more support for Rene’s family, then we’d rather do that than stay silent. At the end of the day, may totoong pamilya at tao kaming gustong matulungan,” the business said. "We are truly thankful to La Salle Zobel for opening its doors and providing them with the opportunity to grow not only as athletes, but also as students and young men of character. Your trust and belief in their potential mean so much to all of us. "We do not take this opportunity lightly. Our boys are committed to working hard, staying humble, and representing the Lasallian community with pride, discipline, and integrity both on and off the court. "A special thank you to Coach Gian Nazario for believing in them and for playing a significant role in helping shape their future. We are honored to entrust our boys to your program. The journey continues. Animo! "Thank you also Phenom Management Head Coach Brody for always being there for us." text.preview: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passed a resolution on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, conferring the Datu Lipus Makapandong Award upon Baterbonia in recognition posthumously of his outstanding achievements, exemplary contributions to basketball, and for bringing honor, prestige, and pride to the province. In the resolution, the provincial government also announced the official retirement of Jersey Number 2 in honor of Baterbonia. The resolution said that the jersey number shall no longer be assigned, worn, or issued to any player participating in Governor’s Cup games and other provincial government-sponsored or sanctioned basketball competitions in Agusan del Sur. The legislative measure added that Baterbonia’s life, achievements, and enduring legacy be permanently recorded in the annals of the province as an example of excellence, discipline, perseverance, humility, leadership, and dedication to sports, serving as an inspiration to present and future generations of Agusanon athletes. Officials ordered furnishing and presentation of a copy of the resolution and a plaque of recognition to Baterbonia’s bereaved family as an expression of the provincial government’s gratitude, admiration, respect, and condolences. The resolution highlighted Baterbonia’s basketball career, including his Most Valuable Player (MVP) award at the Palarong Pambansa 2025 and his role in securing a gold medal for the Philippine team at the ASEAN School Games 2025 in Brunei Darussalam. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Cebu has urged Ateneo de Manila University to help secure the education of the surviving siblings of late student-athlete Rene Baterbonia following the accident that resulted in his death. In a statement issued on June 10, Cebu Archbishop Alberto Uy said that helping ensure the continuation of the siblings' education would be a "fitting tribute" to the dreams of the young man who died during a recent team-building tragedy. "I am confident that the leadership of Ateneo de Manila University also grieves over this heartbreaking loss and shares the desire to seek the truth and accompany the family during this painful journey. Beyond words, concrete acts of solidarity can help ease the burden of those left behind," Uy said. "One meaningful way of honoring Rene's memory would be for Ateneo to help ensure that his siblings are able to complete their education. Those who knew Rene describe him as a young man who dreamed not only for himself but also for the well-being and future of his loved ones. To help fulfill that dream would be a fitting tribute to his life, generosity, and sacrifice," he added. The prelate stressed the need to provide the bereaved family with clear and accurate answers regarding the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. "While no explanation can ever bring Rene back, honesty and transparency can help provide a measure of peace and closure to those who mourn him. If lapses or mistakes were committed, a sincere acknowledgment and apology would be an important step toward healing and rebuilding trust," Uy said. "As we seek truth, accountability, and healing, let us also not forget the power of prayer. Let us pray for the eternal repose of Rene's soul, for healing and strength within the Ateneo community, and for comfort, consolation, and hope for the bereaved Baterbonia family during this time of profound grief," he added. articles.description: Viral posts linking student-athlete Rene Baterbonia's death to a forensic report claims blunt-force traumatic injuries were the cause of death. This is not true.

text.preview: Forensic findings of Rene Baterbonia showing paddle marks, a swollen scrotum, self-defense injuries, and blunt-force traumatic injuries from hazing as cause of death. NBI forensic expert Dr. Rene Cam clarified the result shown in the forensic findings belongs to a PDL who died in Cebu City jail due to hazing on April 26, not that of the Ateneo Blue Eagles player. Multiple graphics and reels are circulating on Facebook and Threads, linking the death of Ateneo student-athlete Rene Clert “Bobet” Baterbonia to preliminary forensic findings of a corpse with paddle marks, a swollen scrotum, self-defense injuries, and signs of blunt-force trauma. This is false. These findings, supposedly disclosed by National Bureau of Investigation forensic expert Dr. Rene Cam in an interview, are not those of Baterbonia who drowned in Dipaculao, Aurora, during a team-building activity on June 8. They belong to a 37-year-old man deprived of liberty who died in the Cebu City jail last April 26. articles.title: FACT CHECK: Baste Duterte did NOT cover transport costs of Baterbonia’s remains
articles.description: Multiple Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte covered all the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia to Agusan del Sur. These posts are false.

text.preview: Sebastian Duterte personally covered the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia from Manila to Agusan del Sur. Ateneo de Manila University provided the private plane to transport the remains of Baterbonia and shouldered funeral and wake expenses. The local government of Davao City, not Duterte, extended assistance for his family’s other needs. At least 13 Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte covered all the expenses in transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) Blue Eagles cager Rene “Bobet” Baterbonia to his hometown in Agusan del Sur. These are false. The earliest copy of the post from an FB user, with a graphic containing a side-by-side photo of Baterbonia and Duterte, was published on June 20. The caption reads: “ HINDI PALA DAW ATENEO ANG SUMAGOT PARA MAIUWI ANG MGA LABI NI RENE BATERBONIA SA TALACOGON 😭” (So it turns out that Ateneo wasn’t the one who covered the expenses to bring Rene Baterbonia’s remains home to Talacogon. 😭😭) The claim was further bolstered with the inclusion of a portion of Ateneo de Davao’s basketball coach Jess Evangelio’s statement expressing his gratitude to Duterte and the local government of Davao City. He said: “We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Sebastian ‘Baste’ Duterte for extending assistance from Manila to Davao and all the way to Talacogon. Your support helped ease the burden on Rene’s family and ensured that he was brought home with dignity and honor. – Coach Jess” While the local government of Davao City helped with the accommodation, food, and transportation of Baterbonia’s family from Davao City to Agusan del Sur, it was Ateneo that provided the plane to transport the remains of the student-athlete. He said: “We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Sebastian ‘Baste’ Duterte for extending assistance from Manila to Davao and all the way to Talacogon. Your support helped ease the burden on Rene’s family and ensured that he was brought home with dignity and honor. – Coach Jess” While the local government of Davao City helped with the accommodation, food, and transportation of Baterbonia’s family from Davao City to Agusan del Sur, it was Ateneo that provided the plane to transport the remains of the student-athlete. article.description: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage.

text.preview: The Provincial Government of Agusan del Sur has declared the late basketball player Rene Clert Baterbonia as an “AgSurnon Sports Icon” in recognition of his achievements and contributions to sports and the promotion of the province on the national and international stage. The Sangguniang Panlalawigan passed a resolution on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, conferring the Datu Lipus Makapandong Award upon Baterbonia in recognition posthumously of his outstanding achievements, exemplary contributions to basketball, and for bringing honor, prestige, and pride to the province. In the resolution, the provincial government also announced the official retirement of Jersey Number 2 in honor of Baterbonia. The resolution said that the jersey number shall no longer be assigned, worn, or issued to any player participating in Governor’s Cup games and other provincial government-sponsored or sanctioned basketball competitions in Agusan del Sur. The legislative measure added that Baterbonia’s life, achievements, and enduring legacy be permanently recorded in the annals of the province as an example of excellence, discipline, perseverance, humility, leadership, and dedication to sports, serving as an inspiration to present and future generations of Agusanon athletes. Officials ordered furnishing and presentation of a copy of the resolution and a plaque of recognition to Baterbonia’s bereaved family as an expression of the provincial government’s gratitude, admiration, respect, and condolences. The resolution highlighted Baterbonia’s basketball career, including his Most Valuable Player (MVP) award at the Palarong Pambansa 2025 and his role in securing a gold medal for the Philippine team at the ASEAN School Games 2025 in Brunei Darussalam. article.description: The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Cebu has urged Ateneo de Manila University to help secure the education of the surviving siblings of late student-athlete Rene Baterbonia following the accident that resulted in his death.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Cebu has urged Ateneo de Manila University to help secure the education of the surviving siblings of late student-athlete Rene Baterbonia following the accident that resulted in his death. In a statement issued on June 10, Cebu Archbishop Alberto Uy said that helping ensure the continuation of the siblings' education would be a "fitting tribute" to the dreams of the young man who died during a recent team-building tragedy. "I am confident that the leadership of Ateneo de Manila University also grieves over this heartbreaking loss and shares the desire to seek the truth and accompany the family during this painful journey. Beyond words, concrete acts of solidarity can help ease the burden of those left behind," Uy said. "One meaningful way of honoring Rene's memory would be for Ateneo to help ensure that his siblings are able to complete their education. Those who knew Rene describe him as a young man who dreamed not only for himself but also for the well-being and future of his loved ones. To help fulfill that dream would be a fitting tribute to his life, generosity, and sacrifice," he added. The prelate stressed the need to provide the bereaved family with clear and accurate answers regarding the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. "While no explanation can ever bring Rene back, honesty and transparency can help provide a measure of peace and closure to those who mourn him. articles.description: Multiple Facebook posts claim that Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte covered all the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia to Agusan del Sur. These posts are false.

text.preview: Sebastian Duterte personally covered the expenses of transporting the remains of Ateneo de Manila University Blue Eagles cager Rene Baterbonia from Manila to Agusan del Sur. Ateneo de Manila University provided the private plane to transport the remains of Baterbonia and shouldered funeral and wake expenses. The caption reads: “ HINDI PALA DAW ATENEO ANG SUMAGOT PARA MAIUWI ANG MGA LABI NI RENE BATERBONIA SA TALACOGON 😭” (So it turns out that Ateneo wasn’t the one who covered the expenses to bring Rene Baterbonia’s remains home to Talacogon. 😭😭) The claim was further bolstered with the inclusion of a portion of Ateneo de Davao’s basketball coach Jess Evangelio’s statement expressing his gratitude to Duterte and the local government of Davao City. He said: “We would also like to express our heartfelt gratitude to Mayor Sebastian ‘Baste’ Duterte for extending assistance from Manila to Davao and all the way to Talacogon. Your support helped ease the burden on Rene’s family and ensured that he was brought home with dignity and honor. – Coach Jess” While the local government of Davao City helped with the accommodation, food, and transportation of Baterbonia’s family from Davao City to Agusan del Sur, it was Ateneo that provided the plane to transport the remains of the student-athlete. Rene’s parents, Rovelyn Baterbonia and Rene Baterbonia Sr., were present at the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball matches on Wednesday and visited UST ahead of its game against De La Salle University. Growling Tigers head coach Pido Jarencio revealed that the Baterbonias decided to visit the team after Rovelyn found comfort in seeing UST forward Koji Buenaflor, whom the family felt bore similarities to Rene. “Yung mother, pumunta sa amin,” said Jarencio after their 80-75 win over La Salle. “Pumunta kay Koji kasi parang lookalike ni Rene. However, before the UST-La Salle match, the Baterbonias moved from the lower box section to the seats behind the Tigers’ bench. It was also around that time that they visited UST’s dugout. “Hindi kami pumapapel, or nag ga-grandstanding, basta pinuntahan kami,” shared Jarencio. “Si Koji, naaalala nila na parang anak nila, kaya kami naman, yun lang ang nao-offer namin sa kanila.” After the Baterbonias shared moments with the Growling Tigers, Jarencio said UST would dedicate its UAAP Season 89 campaign to the family. “Sinabi ko lang naman sa kanya, nandito kayo, ide-dedicate namin lahat ng games namin para sa anak niyo, kay Rene, so tuwang-tuwa yung nanay,” shared Jarencio. “Every game is dedicated kay Rene Baterbonia. The business said it is their “small gesture of support for his family,” lamenting Baterbonia’s death, whom they said was a “young athlete with a bright future.” “Whether it’s a Seiko, Grand Seiko, G-Shock, Citizen, or any watch from our collection, a portion of every successful sale will go directly to Rene’s family,” the shop said in an announcement on Thursday, June 11. “This is not a marketing campaign. This is simply our way of giving back and extending help during a difficult time,” the business added. The business also defended its initiative in the comments section, saying it was not “milking” Baterbonia’s death for profit. “Hindi namin ‘pinagkakakitaan’ ‘yung pagkamatay ng bata. We were already selling watches before this happened, and we will continue selling watches after. The difference now is that part of our earnings will go directly to Rene’s family to help during a difficult time,” it said. “Fundraising through businesses has existed for YEARS. Restaurants, brands, sports teams, and even international companies do donation drives tied to sales because it helps raise bigger amounts using their platform and audience. Hindi porket business ‘yung tumutulong, ‘marketing strategy’ agad,” it added. “If helping while using our reach means more support for Rene’s family, then we’d rather do that than stay silent. At the end of the day, may totoong pamilya at tao kaming gustong matulungan,” the business said. The shop also shared screenshots of its GCash transactions with Rovelyn Baterbonia , Rene’s mother, as proof that the donations had been sent. NBI forensic expert Dr. Rene Cam clarified the result shown in the forensic findings belongs to a PDL who died in Cebu City jail due to hazing on April 26, not that of the Ateneo Blue Eagles player.

Multiple graphics and reels are circulating on Facebook and Threads, linking the death of Ateneo student-athlete Rene Clert “Bobet” Baterbonia to preliminary forensic findings of a corpse with paddle marks, a swollen scrotum, self-defense injuries, and signs of blunt-force trauma.
This is false.

These findings, supposedly disclosed by National Bureau of Investigation forensic expert Dr. Rene Cam in an interview, are not those of Baterbonia who drowned in Dipaculao, Aurora, during a team-building activity on June 8.
They belong to a 37-year-old man deprived of liberty who died in the Cebu City jail last April 26.

passages.text: These misleading posts surfaced five days after the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group Director Maj.
Gen. Robert Morico II announced on July 15 that they were looking into possible homicide or hazing for the deaths of Baterbonia and his teammate, Divine Adili.
Several FB pages and users have since shared the false graphics and reels, prompting Cam to clarify on GMA Regional News on July 9 that he did not conduct Baterbonia’s autopsy.
He explained that the forensic findings circulating online are from the autopsy of another person.
Baterbonia’s Certificate of Post-Mortem Examination lists his cause of death was asphyxia by drowning .
As of press time, authorities have said that the investigation into the circumstances surrounding Baterbonia’s death remains ongoing.

Published by FB pages X Tian Vlog (created June 19, 2019), NewsRadar PH (created September 15, 2023), Gras Ya Vlog (created April 3, 2010), Tita Ni Kurt Vlogs (created July 11, 2011), and several other FB accounts, these posts have collectively garnered over 162,853 reactions;
40,143 comments;
and 27,402 shares.
